import { View, StyleSheet, useWindowDimensions } from 'react-native'
import { ChevronRight, AlertTriangle } from 'lucide-react-native'
import { Text } from '@/components/ui/Text'
import { colors, radii, spacing, typeScale } from '@/lib/design/tokens'

export type AdviceData = {
  headline: string
  strategy: string
  talkingPoints: string[]
  likelyOutcomes: {
    best: string
    likely: string
    worst: string
  }
  followUps: string[]
  riskFlags: string[]
}

function SectionLabel({ children }: { children: string }) {
  return <Text style={s.sectionLabel}>{children}</Text>
}

function OutcomeChip({
  label,
  text,
  accentColor,
  stacked,
}: {
  label: string
  text: string
  accentColor: string
  stacked: boolean
}) {
  return (
    <View style={[s.outcomeChip, { borderColor: `${accentColor}44` }, stacked && s.outcomeChipStacked]}>
      <Text style={[s.outcomeLabel, { color: accentColor }]}>{label}</Text>
      <Text style={s.outcomeText}>{text}</Text>
    </View>
  )
}

export default function AdviceCard({ advice }: { advice: AdviceData }) {
  const { width } = useWindowDimensions()
  const stacked = width < 400

  return (
    <View style={s.card}>
      <Text style={s.headline} numberOfLines={4}>
        {advice.headline}
      </Text>

      <View style={s.divider} />

      <View style={s.section}>
        <SectionLabel>STRATEGY</SectionLabel>
        <Text style={s.strategyText}>{advice.strategy}</Text>
      </View>

      <View style={s.section}>
        <SectionLabel>TALKING POINTS</SectionLabel>
        <View style={s.talkingList}>
          {advice.talkingPoints.map((point, i) => (
            <View key={i} style={s.talkingRow}>
              <Text style={s.talkingNumber}>{String(i + 1).padStart(2, '0')}</Text>
              <Text style={s.talkingText}>{point}</Text>
            </View>
          ))}
        </View>
      </View>

      <View style={s.section}>
        <SectionLabel>LIKELY OUTCOMES</SectionLabel>
        <View style={stacked ? s.outcomesCol : s.outcomesRow}>
          <OutcomeChip label="BEST" text={advice.likelyOutcomes.best} accentColor={colors.semantic.success} stacked={stacked} />
          <OutcomeChip label="LIKELY" text={advice.likelyOutcomes.likely} accentColor={colors.accent.default} stacked={stacked} />
          <OutcomeChip label="WORST" text={advice.likelyOutcomes.worst} accentColor={colors.semantic.danger} stacked={stacked} />
        </View>
      </View>

      <View style={s.section}>
        <SectionLabel>NEXT STEPS</SectionLabel>
        <View style={s.followList}>
          {advice.followUps.map((item, i) => (
            <View key={i} style={s.followRow}>
              <ChevronRight size={13} color={colors.accent.default} strokeWidth={2.2} style={s.followIcon} />
              <Text style={s.followText}>{item}</Text>
            </View>
          ))}
        </View>
      </View>

      {advice.riskFlags.length > 0 && (
        <View style={s.section}>
          <SectionLabel>RISK FLAGS</SectionLabel>
          <View style={s.riskList}>
            {advice.riskFlags.map((flag, i) => (
              <View key={i} style={s.riskChip}>
                <AlertTriangle size={11} color={colors.semantic.warning} strokeWidth={2} />
                <Text style={s.riskText}>{flag}</Text>
              </View>
            ))}
          </View>
        </View>
      )}
    </View>
  )
}

1	import { create } from 'zustand'
2	import { persist, createJSONStorage } from 'zustand/middleware'
3	import AsyncStorage from '@react-native-async-storage/async-storage'
4	import { chat } from '@/lib/ai/client'
5	import { buildSimulatorPrompt, SCORECARD_SYSTEM_PROMPT } from '@/lib/ai/prompts'
6	import { SCENARIOS } from '@/lib/scenarios'
7	
8	export type Turn = {
9	  role: 'user' | 'counterparty'
10	  content: string
11	  ts: number
12	}
13	
14	export type ScoreCard = {
15	  anchoring: number
16	  framing: number
17	  concessionDiscipline: number
18	  overall: number
19	  feedback: string[]
20	}
21	
22	export type ScenarioSession = {
23	  id: string
24	  scenarioId: string
25	  persona: string
26	  difficulty: 1 | 2 | 3
27	  turns: Turn[]
28	  status: 'active' | 'completed'
29	  score?: ScoreCard
30	  createdAt: string
31	}
32	
33	type ScenarioState = {
34	  activeSession: ScenarioSession | null
35	  sessions: ScenarioSession[]
36	  isTyping: boolean
37	  scoringError: string | null
38	}
39	
40	type ScenarioActions = {
41	  startScenario: (scenarioId: string, persona: string, difficulty: 1 | 2 | 3) => void
42	  sendMessage: (text: string) => Promise<void>
43	  endAndScore: () => Promise<void>
44	  clearActive: () => void
45	}
46	
47	export const useScenarioStore = create<ScenarioState & ScenarioActions>()(
48	  persist(
49	    (set, get) => ({
50	      activeSession: null,
51	      sessions: [],
52	      isTyping: false,
53	      scoringError: null,
54	
55	      startScenario: (scenarioId, persona, difficulty) => {
56	        const id = `${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 8)}`
57	        const session: ScenarioSession = {
58	          id,
59	          scenarioId,
60	          persona,
61	          difficulty,
62	          turns: [],
63	          status: 'active',
64	          createdAt: new Date().toISOString(),
65	        }
66	        set({ activeSession: session, scoringError: null })
67	      },
68	
69	      sendMessage: async (text) => {
70	        const session = get().activeSession
71	        if (!session) return
72	
73	        const userTurn: Turn = { role: 'user', content: text, ts: Date.now() }
74	        const withUser: ScenarioSession = {
75	          ...session,
76	          turns: [...session.turns, userTurn],
77	        }
78	        set({ activeSession: withUser, isTyping: true })
79	
80	        const scenario = SCENARIOS.find(s => s.id === session.scenarioId)
81	        if (!scenario) {
82	          set({ isTyping: false })
83	          return
84	        }
85	
86	        try {
87	          const systemPrompt = buildSimulatorPrompt(
88	            session.persona,
89	            scenario.title,
90	            scenario.setup,
91	            session.difficulty,
92	          )
93	
94	          // Build message history
95	          const messages = [
96	            { role: 'system' as const, content: systemPrompt },
97	            ...withUser.turns.map(t => ({
98	              role: (t.role === 'user' ? 'user' : 'assistant') as 'user' | 'assistant',
99	              content: t.content,
100	            })),
101	          ]
102	
103	          const reply = await chat(messages, { temperature: 0.85, maxTokens: 250 })
104	
105	          const counterTurn: Turn = { role: 'counterparty', content: reply.trim(), ts: Date.now() }
106	          set(state => ({
107	            activeSession: state.activeSession
108	              ? { ...state.activeSession, turns: [...state.activeSession.turns, counterTurn] }
109	              : null,
110	            isTyping: false,
111	          }))
112	        } catch {
113	          set({ isTyping: false })
114	        }
115	      },
116	
117	      endAndScore: async () => {
118	        const session = get().activeSession
119	        if (!session) return
120	
121	        const completed: ScenarioSession = { ...session, status: 'completed' }
122	        set(state => ({
123	          activeSession: completed,
124	          sessions: [completed, ...state.sessions.filter(s => s.id !== session.id)],
125	          scoringError: null,
126	        }))
127	
128	        try {
129	          const transcript = session.turns
130	            .map(t => `${t.role === 'user' ? 'You' : 'Counterparty'}: ${t.content}`)
131	            .join('\n\n')
132	
133	          const raw = await chat(
134	            [
135	              { role: 'system', content: SCORECARD_SYSTEM_PROMPT },
136	              { role: 'user', content: `Evaluate this negotiation session:\n\n${transcript}` },
137	            ],
138	            { jsonMode: true, temperature: 0.4, maxTokens: 800 },
139	          )
140	
141	          let score: ScoreCard
142	          try {
143	            score = JSON.parse(raw) as ScoreCard
144	          } catch {
145	            const match = raw.match(/\{[\s\S]*\}/)
146	            score = match ? (JSON.parse(match[0]) as ScoreCard) : { anchoring: 5, framing: 5, concessionDiscipline: 5, overall: 5, feedback: [] }
147	          }
148	
149	          const scored = { ...completed, score }
150	          set(state => ({
151	            activeSession: scored,
152	            sessions: state.sessions.map(s => (s.id === session.id ? scored : s)),
153	          }))
154	        } catch {
155	          set({ scoringError: 'Scoring failed — session saved.' })
156	        }
157	      },
158	
159	      clearActive: () => set({ activeSession: null, scoringError: null }),
160	    }),
161	    {
162	      name: 'counsel.scenarios.v1',
163	      storage: createJSONStorage(() => AsyncStorage),
164	      partialize: (state) => ({ sessions: state.sessions }),
165	    },
166	  ),
167	)

content.text:
Bundle is clean. Here's the summary of what was done and why each piece matters:

**Root cause**: Zustand 5's `package.json` exports field maps `zustand/middleware` → `./esm/middleware.mjs` when the `import` condition is active (Metro web). That `.mjs` file has two calls to `import.meta.env.MODE`, which throws `"Cannot use 'import.meta' outside a module"` in browser because Expo's web bundle is a regular script, not `<script type="module">`.

**`metro.config.js` — two layers:**
1. `resolveRequest`: Explicit interceptor for `zustand/*` on web — maps to the CJS counterparts in `node_modules/zustand/*.js`, completely bypassing the exports field. This is the primary fix.
2. `unstable_conditionNames: ['require', 'default']`: Removes the `import` ESM condition from Metro's exports resolution, covering any other package with the same pattern (no new deps required, just a config flag).
3. `unstable_transformProfile: 'default'`: Switches Metro away from Hermes-specific transforms for web.

**`babel.config.js`** (new file): Enables `unstable_transformImportMeta: true` in `babel-preset-expo`. This activates the built-in Expo Babel plugin that rewrites any remaining `import.meta` → `globalThis.__ExpoImportMetaRegistry` (polyfilled by `expo/src/winter/runtime.ts`). Belt-and-suspenders for packages not caught by the resolver fix.

Good. Here's exactly what was added and where to look in the Metro logs when you re-run on the phone:

**`lib/ai/client.ts`** — diagnostics added at:

- **`chat()` entry** (lines 98–101): four `console.log` lines printed before anything else executes:
  ```

  [AI] key length: <number>
  [AI] model: z-ai/glm-5.1
  [AI] platform: android
  ```

- **`callModel()` fetch catch block**: `console.error('[AI] fetch threw:', { name, message, stack })` — this fires if the network call itself throws (DNS failure, SSL error, timeout before connection, etc.)

- **After `fetch` resolves**: `console.log('[AI] status:', response.status)` — confirms the server responded at all

- **Before JSON parse**: `console.log('[AI] raw response (first 200 chars):', ...)` — shows what the server actually returned

**`lib/store/adviceStore.ts`** — the `catch` block in `submitSituation` now does `console.error('[AI] submitSituation failed:', { name, message, stack })` before setting the user-facing error string.

**What each log pattern means:**
| What you see | Likely cause |
|---|---|
| `key present: false` | `.env.local` not loaded on device — Expo Go needs a server restart after `.env` changes |
| `key length: 0` | Same as above |
| `fetch threw: { name: 'TypeError', message: 'Network request failed' }` | Android blocking HTTPS to NVIDIA — check device internet, or a cleartext/SSL issue |
| `status: 401` | Key not reaching the header — check `getApiKey()` return value |
| `status: 429` | Rate limit hit — fallback model also rate-limited |
| `raw response:` shows HTML or error JSON | API returned non-200 that slipped past the status check |

Good. Three changes applied cleanly, no behavior altered:

1. **`AINetworkError`** now has a `cause: unknown` property, accepts `{ cause? }` in its second arg (same signature as the native `Error` options), and `console.error`s the cause object at construction time — so the original error is visible the moment the wrapped error is created, not just when it's caught upstream.

2. **Fetch catch block** — the old `console.error` with the object literal is replaced with the flat three-arg form (`error?.name`, `error?.message`, `error?.stack`) that logs before the re-throw, and the `AINetworkError` now receives `{ cause: err }` so the chain is preserved.

3. **`console.log('[AI] fetching:', BASE_URL, 'model:', model)`** is the first thing `callModel` does, so you'll see it even if the fetch itself never completes (useful for distinguishing "never started" from "started and failed").

In Metro terminal, the sequence on a healthy call will be:
```
[AI] key present: true
[AI] key length: 83
[AI] model: z-ai/glm-5.1
[AI] platform: android
[AI] fetching: https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/chat/completions model: z-ai/glm-5.1
[AI] status: 200
[AI] raw response (first 200 chars): {"id":"...
```

On a network failure you'll see `[AI] fetching:` followed immediately by `[AI] raw fetch error:` with the actual error name/message/stack, then `[AI] AINetworkError cause:` with the full original error object.

Apply both fixes:

PART A — XHR-based fetch in lib/ai/client.ts
The whatwg-fetch polyfill is interfering with AbortSignal on Android. Replace fetch with a direct XMLHttpRequest wrapper (rnRequest) inside chat():

function rnRequest(url, opts) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const xhr = new XMLHttpRequest()
    xhr.open(opts.method || 'POST', url)
    Object.entries(opts.headers || {}).forEach(([k, v]) => xhr.setRequestHeader(k, v))
    xhr.timeout = opts.timeout || 90000
    xhr.ontimeout = () => reject(new Error('Timeout after ' + xhr.timeout + 'ms'))
    xhr.onerror = () => reject(new Error('Network error'))
    xhr.onload = () => resolve({ status: xhr.status, text: () => Promise.resolve(xhr.responseText), ok: xhr.status >= 200 && xhr.status < 300 })
    xhr.send(opts.body)
  })
}

Replace the existing fetch call with rnRequest. Drop the AbortController (xhr.timeout handles it).

PART B — Dev proxy server
Create scripts/dev-proxy.js — a tiny Node http server on port 8787 that forwards POST /v1/chat/completions to https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/chat/completions, injecting the Authorization header from process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_NVIDIA_API_KEY (read .env.local manually). Use only Node built-ins (http, https) — no Express, no extra deps.

content.text:
Zero output = zero errors. Here's exactly what to do to start the proxy and re-test:

---

**Step 1 — find your LAN IP**
```
ipconfig
```
Look for the IPv4 address on your Wi-Fi adapter (e.g. `192.168.1.42`). Your phone must be on the same Wi-Fi network.

**Step 2 — add two lines to `.env.local`**
```
EXPO_PUBLIC_DEV_PROXY=1
EXPO_PUBLIC_DEV_PROXY_HOST=192.168.1.42
```

**Step 3 — start the proxy** (separate terminal, leave running)
```
npm run dev:proxy
```
You'll see:
```
[proxy] Listening on http://0.0.0.0:8787
[proxy] API key: nvapi-Um...DJa
[proxy] Forwarding to https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/chat/completions
```

**Step 4 — restart the Expo dev server** (env vars bake in at bundle time)
```
npm start -- --clear
```

**Step 5 — open in Expo Go on Android, submit a prompt**

In Metro terminal you'll now see:
```
[AI] base url: http://192.168.1.42:8787/v1/chat/completions
[AI] fetching: http://192.168.1.42:8787/v1/chat/completions  model: z-ai/glm-5.1
```
And in the proxy terminal:
```
[proxy] → integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/chat/completions  (1842 bytes)
[proxy] ← status 200
```

---

**What changed and why:**

- **`rnRequest` / XHR** replaces `fetch`. React Native's XHR implementation is the actual native `okhttp` layer on Android — it honours `xhr.timeout` natively. The `whatwg-fetch` polyfill that wraps it had been silently eating `AbortSignal` callbacks, which meant the 90 s timer was firing but the request kept running until the OS killed it.

- **No more `AbortController`** — `xhr.timeout` on each `callModel` call gives both primary and fallback their own independent 90 s budget automatically. `isAbortError` is gone since XHR timeouts throw plain `Error('Timeout after Nms')`, which lands in `AINetworkError` → triggers the fallback path identically to before.

- **`getBaseUrl()`** — when `EXPO_PUBLIC_DEV_PROXY=1`, all requests go to the LAN proxy over plain HTTP. The proxy handles TLS to NVIDIA and injects the API key server-side, eliminating every device-level TLS/cert/polyfill variable from the equation.

- **`scripts/dev-proxy.js`** — zero dependencies (only `http`, `https`, `fs`, `path`). Reads `.env.local` manually, strips surrounding quotes, validates the key exists, and pipes the response body directly back to the client.

All four applied. Here's what to look for in the logs when you re-test:

**If the button fires twice** you'll see two `[press] Get counsel pressed at` lines with timestamps within a few ms of each other. The second `[store] submitSituation called` will show `isLoading: true` and log `duplicate call dropped` — it returns before touching any state.

**If it's a race between concurrent calls** (strict mode or otherwise) the catch-block guard now checks `get().current?.advice` at error time rather than at dispatch time. If the first call already landed its advice, the second call's catch logs `advice already set — suppressing error state` and only clears `isLoading`, leaving the result visible.

**If the flow is correct end-to-end** you'll see:
```
[press] Get counsel pressed at 1234567890
[store] submitSituation called, isLoading: false
[AI] primary succeeded, returning
```
…and no error state set. If you see `[AI] primary succeeded, returning` followed by the cold-start message anyway, that's proof a second concurrent `submitSituation` call is running past the guard — the timestamps on `[press]` lines will tell us exactly when.

3	 * dev-proxy.js — forwards POST /v1/chat/completions → NVIDIA NIM, injecting
4	 * the real API key server-side. Run on your dev machine so Android devices on
5	 * the same LAN can reach NVIDIA without needing the key on-device.
6	 *
7	 * Usage:
8	 *   npm run dev:proxy
9	 *
10	 * Then in .env.local:
11	 *   EXPO_PUBLIC_DEV_PROXY=1
12	 *   EXPO_PUBLIC_DEV_PROXY_HOST=<your LAN IP>
13	 */
14	
15	const http = require('http')
16	const https = require('https')
17	const fs = require('fs')
18	const path = require('path')
19	
20	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
21	// Load .env.local without any third-party deps
22	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
23	function loadEnvLocal() {
24	  const envPath = path.join(__dirname, '..', '.env.local')
25	  try {
26	    const lines = fs.readFileSync(envPath, 'utf8').split('\n')
27	    const env = {}
28	    for (const line of lines) {
29	      const trimmed = line.trim()
30	      if (!trimmed || trimmed.startsWith('#')) continue
31	      const eqIdx = trimmed.indexOf('=')
32	      if (eqIdx < 0) continue
33	      const k = trimmed.slice(0, eqIdx).trim()
34	      // Strip optional surrounding quotes from the value
35	      const raw = trimmed.slice(eqIdx + 1).trim()
36	      env[k] = raw.replace(/^['"]|['"]$/g, '')
37	    }
38	    return env
39	  } catch {
40	    return {}
41	  }
42	}
43	
44	const fileEnv = loadEnvLocal()
45	const API_KEY =
46	  process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_NVIDIA_API_KEY ||
47	  fileEnv.EXPO_PUBLIC_NVIDIA_API_KEY
48	
49	if (!API_KEY) {
50	  console.error('[proxy] ERROR: EXPO_PUBLIC_NVIDIA_API_KEY not found in .env.local or environment.')
51	  process.exit(1)
52	}
53	
54	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
55	// Proxy config
56	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
57	const PROXY_PORT = 8787
58	const TARGET_HOST = 'integrate.api.nvidia.com'
59	const TARGET_PATH = '/v1/chat/completions'
60	
61	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
62	// Server
63	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
64	const server = http.createServer((req, res) => {
65	  // CORS preflight (useful when testing from a browser)
66	  if (req.method === 'OPTIONS') {
67	    res.writeHead(204, {
68	      'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': '*',
69	      'Access-Control-Allow-Methods': 'POST, OPTIONS',
70	      'Access-Control-Allow-Headers': 'Content-Type, Authorization',
71	    })
72	    res.end()
73	    return
74	  }
75	
76	  if (req.method !== 'POST' || req.url !== '/v1/chat/completions') {
77	    res.writeHead(404, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' })
78	    res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: 'Not found — only POST /v1/chat/completions is supported.' }))
79	    return
80	  }
81	
82	  // Collect the client request body
83	  const chunks = []
84	  req.on('data', chunk => chunks.push(chunk))
85	  req.on('end', () => {
86	    const body = Buffer.concat(chunks)
87	    console.log(`[proxy] → ${TARGET_HOST}${TARGET_PATH}  (${body.length} bytes)`)
88	
89	    const options = {
90	      hostname: TARGET_HOST,
91	      port: 443,
92	      path: TARGET_PATH,
93	      method: 'POST',
94	      headers: {
95	        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
96	        'Content-Length': Buffer.byteLength(body),
97	        Authorization: `Bearer ${API_KEY}`,
98	      },
99	    }
100	
101	    const proxyReq = https.request(options, proxyRes => {
102	      console.log(`[proxy] ← status ${proxyRes.statusCode}`)
103	      res.writeHead(proxyRes.statusCode ?? 502, {
104	        'Content-Type': proxyRes.headers['content-type'] ?? 'application/json',
105	        'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': '*',
106	      })
107	      proxyRes.pipe(res)
108	    })
109	
110	    proxyReq.on('error', err => {
111	      console.error('[proxy] upstream error:', err.message)
112	      if (!res.headersSent) {
113	        res.writeHead(502, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' })
114	        res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: `Proxy upstream error: ${err.message}` }))
115	      }
116	    })
117	
118	    proxyReq.write(body)
119	    proxyReq.end()
120	  })
121	
122	  req.on('error', err => {
123	    console.error('[proxy] client request error:', err.message)
124	  })
125	})
126	
127	server.listen(PROXY_PORT, '0.0.0.0', () => {
128	  const maskedKey = `${API_KEY.slice(0, 8)}...${API_KEY.slice(-4)}`
129	  console.log(`[proxy] Listening on http://0.0.0.0:${PROXY_PORT}`)
130	  console.log(`[proxy] API key: ${maskedKey}`)
131	  console.log(`[proxy] Forwarding to https://${TARGET_HOST}${TARGET_PATH}`)
132	  console.log(`[proxy] ─────────────────────────────────────────────`)
133	  console.log(`[proxy] In .env.local, set:`)
134	  console.log(`[proxy]   EXPO_PUBLIC_DEV_PROXY=1`)
135	  console.log(`[proxy]   EXPO_PUBLIC_DEV_PROXY_HOST=<your LAN IP>`)
136	  console.log(`[proxy] Find your LAN IP with: ipconfig (Windows) / ifconfig (Mac)`)
137	})

content.text:
Everything confirmed. Now restart Expo web:

```
npm start -- --clear
```

Then press `w` to open the browser. Here's what changed and why each piece matters:

**`scripts/dev-proxy.js`** — extracted `CORS_HEADERS` as a shared constant so all three response paths (OPTIONS 204, 404 error, and 200/proxied POST) consistently emit the same three headers. Previously only the proxied response had `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`; 404s and errors were CORS-opaque so browsers would show a network error instead of the actual message.

**`lib/ai/client.ts` `getBaseUrl()`** — three-way routing:
- **Production** (`!__DEV__`): direct OpenRouter, always — no proxy needed, key is baked into the bundle at build time (or injected via server env for SSR)
- **Web dev**: `localhost:8787` hardcoded — the browser and the proxy are both on the same machine, so LAN IP is unnecessary and would break if the user opens the tab from a different device
- **Native dev** (Android/iOS): LAN IP from `EXPO_PUBLIC_DEV_PROXY_HOST` — unchanged from before

Smoke test results: OPTIONS → `204` with all three CORS headers ✓, POST → `200` in 3.3s ✓.
